metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Center Point, AL | Jefferson County
metaDescription: Own mineral rights under land near Center Point, AL? Get a hedged, activity-based cash offer even if the surface is now a subdivision.
heroLead: Center Point grew from farmland into one of Jefferson County's denser residential suburbs over the past several decades, and the minerals underneath a lot of those subdivisions never followed the surface into the sale.
intro: When farm families sold land here for residential development in the 1960s through 1990s, mineral rights were sometimes carved out and kept, either intentionally or as a routine clause the seller barely noticed. Today the surface might be a street of houses, while a scattered mineral interest tied to the original tract still sits with descendants who live nowhere near Center Point at all.
We buy those interests directly once ownership is confirmed, and we've found most owners are surprised to learn the reservation existed at all until they start looking into an old family deed.

sections.heading: A residential surface, a separate mineral history
paragraphs: Center Point's growth means most of the land here no longer looks like the farm or timber tract it once was, but the mineral estate is governed by whatever the original deed said, not by current zoning or subdivision plats. If your family sold surface property in this area, checking whether minerals were reserved is worth doing even decades later.

sections.heading: Where this sits in the Black Warrior play
paragraphs: Center Point sits closer to Jefferson County's urban core than to the coalbed methane fields concentrated farther southwest, so direct drilling activity nearby has been limited. That generally means value here leans more on comparable lease activity than on an existing production record, and we're upfront about that before quoting.

sections.heading: Tracking down an old reservation
paragraphs: We search Jefferson County's deed records for the original transaction on a Center Point-area tract to determine whether a mineral reservation exists, then trace the ownership forward through any subsequent estates to confirm your current share.

faqs.question: The land is a subdivision now. Could my family still own minerals under it?
faqs.answer: Possibly, if a reservation was recorded when the surface was originally sold for development. We check the deed history to confirm before making an offer.

faqs.question: Is there drilling activity right around Center Point?
faqs.answer: This area sits closer to Jefferson County's urban core than to the denser coalbed methane fields farther southwest, so nearby activity has generally been limited.

faqs.question: How do I even know if my family kept mineral rights when we sold?
faqs.answer: We can pull the original recorded deed from Jefferson County's records to check for a mineral reservation clause, even if your family's own copy has been lost.

faqs.question: Does it matter that the current surface owner is a homeowner, not our family?
faqs.answer: No. Mineral ownership is entirely separate from surface ownership once severed, so a current homeowner has no claim to your family's mineral interest.
